..
Issued at 138 AM CDT Wed Sep 23 2026

The bulk of the low to mid level moisture (RAP 1000-500mb RH>70%) is 
over southern SD through NE. This will continue to surge northward 
(thanks to a 25-35kt southerly LLJ) interacting with a weak 
shortwave aloft. Cams indicate this spotty potential for light rain 
across portions of central SD through the James Valley with pops 
diminishing by late morning or so as the shortwave continues to exit 
to the northeast. Cams seem to handle this potential fairly well but 
there is a difference in intensity/coverage area and how far north 
these showers could go in the CWA. So low confidence on who will see 
the rain with NBM highlighting the bulk of this (30-55%) over south 
central SD and southward of the CWA. So pops may need to be adjusted 
through the morning.

The main feature is the negative tilted shortwave that will be over 
MT/WY by 12Z where it will track northeastward through Thursday 
morning, clipping the northern half of SD in the process, with 
southwesterly winds. At the surface, winds will continue out of the 
southeast ahead of its weak surface low moving in over southwestern 
ND this evening with another weak low developing over western SD. 
With this forcing, and ongoing LLJ over central SD pumping in 
moisture, models indicate precip moving in, mainly across north 
central SD mid/late morning to even the midday. NBM is the most 
aggressive with the rain moving in closer to 12Z while HREF mean 
indicates more 15-18Z as ENS a bit slower on the rain timing entering 
with GEPS being the quickest. So low confidence on exact timing. As 
the system tracks northeast, and the low level jet eastward (and 
weakens bit), rain chances also spread a bit eastward. Again HREF 
mean and CAMS really keep this rain spotty along the WAA side of the 
system this afternoon through the evening with the bulk staying
closer to the axis of the trough over ND. NBM is still aggressive
on pops so they may need to be adjusted as well closer to time.
Precip chances and coverage area does increase per CAMS/HREF 
around ~04-06Z (thus increasing confidence) with the bulk of the
pops of 50%+ James Valley and eastward with 80%+ along and east
of the Coteau as drier air will already be moving in over 
central SD on the backside of this system. This is in part to an
increase in southwesterly winds aloft at 700mb (25-30kts) and 
the LLJ strengthening again to around 35-40kts pulling in that 
moisture. During this time PWAT values are forecast to range 
between 1.25-1.5" east of the Mo River and highest eastern SD/MN
which is about 3 standard deviations above climo per NAEFs. EFI
does highlight 0.5 to 0.7 Coteau and eastward with a SOT of 
zero over far SD/ND/MN border meaning most members are near 
reforecast climatology and not expecting anything too anomalous.
Probability of 24hr QPF>0.25", ending 18Z Thursday is 50-90% 
James Valley and eastward, and highest along and east of the 
Coteau. Prob of a half inch is 30-65%, again highest Coteau and 
eastward. A few of the HREF members do show the potential for 
weak thunderstorms as MUCAPE will be up to 750j/kg. However no 
severe weather is expected. Any stronger rain shower or storm 
will lead to the potential of higher QPF. We are also not 
outlooked on ERO so flooding is not expected. As the system 
continues into Canada and dry air spreads eastward Thursday 
morning, pops will continue to diminishes west to east with the 
last of rain exiting eastern SD/MN by mid to late morning.

Dry conditions are then expected through early Thursday evening. 
Chances of precip returns Thursday night across the southern CWA 
with this moisture spreading northward Friday per a south to north 
tracking shortwave from the central plains. It then combines and 
gets absorbed by a negative shortwave trough moving in from the 
southwest (ahead of a large trough sitting over the PacNW). This 
system will then track northeast across the region through Saturday 
morning. The highest pops of 70-85% will be Friday evening through 
Saturday morning, highest James Valley and eastward (thanks to a 
strengthening southerly LLJ). Pops diminish west to east as the 
system moves out by late Saturday morning. Could see another few 
tenths of an inch of rainfall from this. As of now high pressure 
moves in behind it with dry conditions expected for the rest of 
Saturday and Sunday. This unsettled weather pattern setup continues 
with precip chances again early next week.
